bole.text: Bole straight and cylindrical, branchless up to 20 (max 30) m, sometimes fluted, short buttresses up to 2 m high (ICRAF). TTSM: buttresses 1-2.5 m. Useful Tropical Plants (src 1): buttressed or basally swollen for 60-90 cm, unbranched for 9-27 m. Trees become surface-rooted with age.

crown.text: Canopy or subcanopy element of lowland rainforest (Useful Tropical Plants, ICRAF); 'tall tree with dense foliage' (English Wikipedia, src 5).

phenology.fruit: quadrangular woody 4-valved capsule 9-16 cm wide and about as long, falling to the ground; large angular red-brown seeds

bark.colour: light grey to greyish brown or dark brown, sometimes reddish; inner bark red or pinkish brown
bark.text: Flaking into squarish scales or horizontal strips (ICRAF). TTSM fragment: 'usually reddish when older'.

habitat.range: Belize and the Atlantic coast of Central America (and the Costa Rican Pacific watershed) to Panama; Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas, Ecuador, Peru, Brazil; Antilles from Cuba to Trinidad.

notes: Name: the Manual de Plantas de Costa Rica's 2007 Meliaceae treatment (reported by MOBOT, src 3) restricts C. guianensis to a species 'quite rare in Costa Rica'; most Costa Rican populations, presumably including Osa, are C. nicaraguensis (Kenfack's distinction). TTSM, Useful Tropical Plants, Spanish Wikipedia and HVAA treat C. nicaraguensis as a synonym of C. guianensis, and all trait values here come from C. guianensis in the broad sense. TTSM also notes Costa Rican Atlantic and Pacific populations may be different ecotypes. Leaf habit: TTSM 'evergreen or deciduous', Useful Tropical Plants 'semi-deciduous', ICRAF 'deciduous or semi-evergreen'; I mapped this to brevideciduous; no leafless months given. Leaves: paripinnate with a dormant glandular leaflet at the tip, leaflets opposite and entire, very large leaves in the unbranched juvenile stage (ICRAF); no sizes found. Flowering: one short period a year, months not given (ICRAF, UTP). Fruits take 8-12 months to mature; TTSM says harvested May-Aug (region not stated, probably Costa Rica). Seeds float and are dispersed by water; in Costa Rica agoutis scatter-hoard them, and occasionally pigs (ICRAF, UTP). Height: usually up to 35 m, occasionally 55 m (UTP, ICRAF); TTSM up to 60 m. dbh max 200 cm (ICRAF, TTSM 2 m); UTP 180 cm recorded. Light: 'moderately tolerant of shade, but full overhead light is required for fast growth' (UTP). Elevation: usually below 700 m, occasionally to 1000 m (TTSM, UTP); ICRAF 0-1200 m. Animal names as spelled in TTSM (Tayassu tajacu = Pecari tajacu, Agouti paca = Cuniculus paca, 'Hypsiphyla' = Hypsipyla); TTSM says the birds use it for 'food and nesting' without naming the part eaten. Flower colour: ICRAF white; TTSM fragment mentions 'a light pinkish color externally'. Parts of the TTSM PDF are scanned and were only partly readable.
